inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $64M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $36M (financing). Grainger publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: 47.2M shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q) plus ~0.4M dilutive awards = 47.6M fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. Grainger is an active repurchaser (FY2025 $1,045M, H1-2026 $461M), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.0 x ERP ~4.5% = ~8.7% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~3.4% on ~4% debt weight (debt $2.4B vs ~$59B equity) gives ~8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality, tariff and Amazon-Business risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost is inside SG&A (and therefore inside reported EBITDA and OCF), so no lease adjustment is made to the flows and operating lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. total_debt is notes and borrowings only. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: MonotaRO (Japan) is ~50.5% owned and fully consolidated; ~49.5% NCI takes ~$88M of FY2025 net income (consolidated $1,808M vs attributable ~$1,720M), ~3.3% of underlying EBIT. Charged ONCE: folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a leakage add-on (24.5% cash tax + 3.3pp rising to 4.3pp as MonotaRO outgrows the group). No NCI deduction in the bridge. Calibration: FY2025 underlying EBIT ~$2,745M x (1-0.278) = ~$1,980M unlevered attributable NOPAT vs adjusted attributable NI ~$1,915M (39.48 x 48.5M) -- difference is after-tax interest expense (~$68M).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials'), read with owner-fcf-adaptations.md for the NCI, working-capital and lease rules. First valuation of this ticker. Owner FCF = reported FCF 1,331 - SBC incl. withholding taxes 100 - interest income 0 = 1,231 (FY2025). Interest income is not stripped because the company is net DEBT ($1.8B), not net cash. FY2025 GAAP EBIT margin of 13.9% carries ~$250M of Q3-2025 non-recurring charges (adjusted EPS $39.48 vs GAAP $35.47); underlying pre-SBC EBITDA margin was ~17.5%, and the FY2026 driver year is anchored to the raised August-2026 guidance (net sales $19.4-19.7B, operating margin 15.8-16.2%) which includes ~0.2pp from the one-time $43M IEEPA tariff refund that laps in FY2027. Capex is elevated (FY2025 3.8% of sales vs a 2.0-2.5% decade norm) by the DC build-out and tapers to 2.5%. Working capital: as a distributor with receivables + inventory well above payables (net working capital ~19% of sales), growth CONSUMES cash -- wc_capture is negative at -18% of the revenue increase (FY2023-25 observed drag 12-27%). Price is a regular-session close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_10yr_cagr (FY2015-FY2025), cross-checked against the segment mix: High-Touch ~78% at 3-4% + Endless Assortment ~20% at 15%+ blends to ~5.5-6.5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.6% diverges >30% from revenue 8.7% and owner-FCF 7.4%; the equity series is distorted by buybacks (the $1.4B FY2015 repurchase cut book equity by a third, so later CAGRs rebound off a shrunken base) and is NOT used. EPS 5yr CAGR 22.5% is off the FY2020 pandemic trough and is likewise not a run-rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (FY2020 862 -> FY2025 1,231; FY2022 1,006 -> FY2025 1,231) run ~0.3pp below reported-FCF CAGRs, so SBC is not outrunning cash flow; withholding taxes on awards (FY2025 $36M) are included in the owner series. FY2025 owner FCF is depressed by peak DC capex ($684M) and the Q3-2025 charges; H1-2026 owner FCF was ~$830M vs ~$660M in H1-2025.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +9.0% = midpoint of the raised guidance ($19.4-19.7B); H1-2026 was +10.2%. Thereafter blends High-Touch at 3-4% with Endless Assortment at ~15% decaying, fading to 3% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 18.1% pre-SBC EBITDA = guided op margin ~16.0% + D&A 1.85% + SBC 0.36% less a haircut for H2 fade; FY2027 drops 0.2pp as the $43M IEEPA refund laps, then drifts down 0.1pp every other year for Endless Assortment mix dilution net of pricing/leverage.
base.cash_tax_rationale: 24.5% cash tax (FY2023-25 cash taxes paid 606-615M on ~2.4-2.55B pretax) + NCI leakage 3.3pp rising to 4.3pp.
base.capex_rationale: DC build-out (FY2025 3.8%, H1-2026 2.9%) tapers to the 2.5% decade norm by year 5; D&A rises toward 2.1% as the new DCs depreciate.

bull.rationale: Top of FY2026 guidance, Endless Assortment sustains ~20% and MonotaRO NCI leakage therefore rises faster; pricing and DC productivity hold margins up despite mix.

bear.rationale: Bottom of FY2026 guidance (H1 already banked), then a 2027-28 US industrial downturn stalls High-Touch while Amazon Business and category specialists compress price; margin resets toward the FY2022 level (~16%) as the tariff refund laps and cumulative tariff costs are only partly passed through. Lower 15x cap for a slower, more cyclical exit.

scenario_narratives.base: High-Touch Solutions N.A. (78% of sales) grows low-to-mid single digits with the MRO cycle while Endless Assortment (Zoro, MonotaRO) compounds mid-teens off a 20% base, blending to ~6% group growth that fades to 3%. FY2026 lands at the raised guidance midpoint (+9%, ~16% operating margin) and FY2027 gives back the ~0.2pp IEEPA refund; from there Endless Assortment mix dilutes the consolidated margin about 0.1pp every other year, offset only partly by pricing and DC productivity. The 2024-26 DC capex wave tapers to the 2.5% decade norm, and growth continues to consume ~18% of incremental revenue as inventory and receivables. MonotaRO's ~49.5% minority takes a slowly rising slice of NOPAT.
scenario_narratives.bull: Reshoring and a stronger 2026-28 industrial capex cycle lift High-Touch to mid-single-digit growth while Zoro US and MonotaRO sustain ~20%, keeping group growth at 7-8% through 2029. Pricing power in mission-critical safety and maintenance SKUs, DC network productivity and Endless Assortment scale let the consolidated margin rise toward 19% despite mix. Terminal growth 3.5% for a business still gaining share of a fragmented $160-170B market.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 finishes at the bottom of guidance and 2027-28 brings a US manufacturing downturn: High-Touch volumes go flat-to-down, Endless Assortment slows as Amazon Business and category specialists (fasteners, metalworking, safety) undercut price on commoditised SKUs, and price transparency erodes the High-Touch premium. With the tariff refund lapped and cumulative IEEPA costs only partly passed through, the pre-SBC EBITDA margin resets to ~16%, the FY2022 level. Long-run growth settles at 2.5-3% and the exit multiple is capped at 15x for a slower, cyclical distributor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 20%: MRO demand is moderately cyclical, the FY2026 margin is flattered by a one-time tariff refund management says will not recur, and consensus targets sit near the price with a Hold rating. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because it needs High-Touch to re-accelerate AND Endless Assortment to hold ~20% AND margins to expand against mix -- three independent things. No solvency or refinancing risk (net debt/EBITDA ~0.6x, coverage ~30x), so the bear is a margin/cycle case, not a survival case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: SBC and equity-award withholding taxes expensed, share count held flat (buybacks value-neutral), MonotaRO minority charged once through NOPAT leakage, working capital charged as a cash drag on growth, DC capex tapering to norm. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon (8.5%/3.0%) and 20x year-10 FCF; the 15% hurdle entry price rebuilds the terminal value at the hurdle. GWW trades at ~27x forward EPS and ~35-40x trailing owner FCF, so a WACC-discounted DCF sits well below the market -- the gap is the price of the quality/compounder premium the market pays, and the required-return table shows what IRR today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin base: FY2026 guidance includes a one-time $43M IEEPA tariff refund; if underlying margins are lower than the ~18% pre-SBC EBITDA anchored here, every scenario shifts down
Endless Assortment mix: faster-than-modelled growth in the lower-margin segment lifts revenue but dilutes the consolidated margin and raises MonotaRO NCI leakage
Working-capital drag: a distributor's growth consumes cash; the -18% capture is an average of 12-27% observed FY2023-25
Capex normalisation: if the DC build-out does not taper to 2.5% of sales, owner FCF stays ~1pp of revenue lower
Discount rate: value is terminal-heavy; the 8.5% WACC vs a 10.5% house tech default is worth a large share of the per-share value (see sensitivity grid)
Amazon Business / price transparency eroding the High-Touch premium faster than the bear path assumes
